observed_evidence: Reuters reporting based on three sources briefed on pre-summit U.S.-China discussions said Xi Jinping is expected to press Donald Trump to halt Taiwan arms sales under Beijing's interpretation of the 1982 joint communique.
The sources also said China has asked the United States to stop deliveries of weapons already ordered by Taiwan.
A White House official said Trump would make a determination on the new arms-sales package in a fairly short time; no verified U.S. policy change or cancellation had been announced at the cutoff.
semantic_interpretation: This materially raises Taiwan-security policy uncertainty into the Trump-Xi summit but is not evidence that U.S. Taiwan policy or arms-sales law has changed. It can transmit through Taiwan risk premium, defence procurement expectations, USD/TWD and semiconductor geopolitical risk, but no deterministic shock should be applied until policy action is verified.
notes: Reuters-sourced report carried by Taipei Times. No policy outcome is inferred before the summit.
